observation.visible_scene: A brightly lit dance studio with white walls, a dark ceiling with recessed spotlights, a wall-mounted air-conditioning unit, and a full-length mirror wall on the right topped by a continuous light strip. A woman with long dark hair, seen from behind, wears a red sleeveless top, a white fluffy tutu skirt, red leg warmers, red shoes, and a Santa hat. She stands in a wide stance facing the mirror; her mirrored image appears in the glass as a reflection of the same person, not a second dancer. The camera is static throughout (background fixtures, mirror seams, and ceiling lights do not shift).
visible_changes: Arms cycle between two configurations: from t≈0 to t≈0.17 s the left arm is extended horizontally out to the side while the right arm is bent with the hand near the head/hat, with small wrist adjustments; from t≈0.2 to t≈0.63 s both arms lift and are held raised overhead in a wide V; from t≈0.67 to t≈1.03 s the arms drop back to the side-and-head configuration (left arm out, right hand moving around the face); from t≈1.07 s to the end both arms rise overhead again.
The torso sways and rotates slightly in sync with the arm changes, alternating between a more angled posture (one arm out) and a squarer posture facing the mirror (both arms up).

Weight shifts through the legs: the right heel lifts and the right leg straightens during the mid-segment (≈t 0.73–1.03 s), while the left heel rises toward the end (≈t 1.2–1.33 s); knees bend and extend accordingly, but the feet largely stay planted in the same wide stance.
The mirror reflection reproduces every arm, torso, and leg movement as a left-right mirrored image of the same dancer.
No editing cut or jump is visible; the motion is continuous across the whole excerpt, already in progress at the first frame and still ongoing at the last (arms end raised, not lowered).
outside_clip_unknowns: The dance moves before t=0 and after t=1.33 s are not shown, so it is unknown whether the overhead-arm pose at the end is followed by a lowering or a new step.
The music, choreography intent, and whether these arm cycles form a repeating loop cannot be determined from this segment alone.
uncertain_details: Exact finger/hand shapes are blurred in several frames, so the precise hand gestures (e.g., open palm vs. touching the face) are only roughly discernible.
Minor body-position differences between consecutive frames could reflect either the dancer's sway or slight camera/frame jitter; the dominant, reliable motion is the arm cycling.
It is not possible to tell from this crop whether the heel lifts are deliberate steps or weight transfers accompanying the arm movements.
